bench.text: The shop is quiet for eleven minutes before the cooperative's board opens. Renzo spends them where he always does: at the bench.

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: Three things on this bench do not belong. I only have time to chase two.

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: What do I look at first?
Asian Housing & Credit Corp. Under the red FINAL NOTICE stamp, in smaller type: 'Collections Officer: R. Valdez. Tow unit dispatched 12:00 noon. Seizure of leased premises to follow.'

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: Leased premises. Not the bike. The shop.

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: Valdez isn't after a Honda. The Honda is just the door.
The pendulum clock's case is still open from this morning. Under Lola's note, in pencil so faint it is almost not there: 'A.R. 4:17, 3 Hunyo 1998. Hindi na sila tumigil.' They never stopped.

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: A.R. Andres Reyes. Lolo. 'They never stopped.' Who never stopped?
One crate lid is loose. Newspaper, jars, a flour sack, and under them a bus pass to Vigan, dated tomorrow morning, with one name on it. Not Renzo's.

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: She bought one seat. For herself, or for the watch.

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: Keep digging, or go downstairs to Lola?

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: Put it together. Valdez wants the shop. Lolo's note says something never stopped. Lola is packing for Vigan.

bench.speaker: Renzo
bench.text: Whatever 'they' are, she has been outrunning them for twenty-six years, and she has been doing it alone.
Downstairs, a kettle begins to whistle.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: Sit. The board will not open faster because you are standing.
Tanglad and chamomile, in the same chipped cup Renzo has used since he was nine.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: You've been quiet all week, 'La.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: I have been counting. It is not the same as quiet.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: She counts when she's afraid. Jars. Crates. Days.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: Your Lolo used to say a shop is a clock. Every part must agree about what time it is.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: Is that why you stopped them all? So they would agree?

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: That is a clever thing to notice, anak.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: She's offering me one question. Maybe.

options: Say nothing and drink your tea

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: He was a watchmaker the way some men are fishermen. Patient, and a little afraid of the sea.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: The night of the flood in '98 he went out at four in the morning, and he took the old watch. He came back at dawn with the water at his knees and said only: 'Hindi na ito titigil.' It will not stop.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: 'They never stopped.' 'It will not stop.' The same words, twenty-six years apart.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: Packing is not leaving.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: A bus pass to Vigan is leaving.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: ...You read my things.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: They were on the bench.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: Then you have found what I did not hide well enough. One seat, apo. Yours is not yet bought. I wanted to see who would come first: the lenders, or the truth.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: She is testing me. Or protecting me. With Lola there is no difference.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: You are your Lolo's grandson. You know when to leave a gear alone.
The tea is the only warm thing in the shop. For one minute neither of them needs anything else.

lola_tea.speaker: Renzo
lola_tea.text: I will find out what she is hiding. Just not on this cup of tea.

lola_tea.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_tea.text: Go. The board is open. Take what you can carry, and nothing you cannot.

job_avenida.text: Avenida Rizal. Cloth stalls shoulder to shoulder, bolts stacked like sandbags against the rising gutters.

job_avenida.speaker: Aling Cora
job_avenida.text: Reyes! Thank God. Forty bolts of katsa for Divisoria, and the lorry driver has gone to wait out the rain somewhere dry and stupid.

job_avenida.speaker: Renzo
job_avenida.text: Forty bolts on a Honda Beat?

job_avenida.speaker: Aling Cora
job_avenida.text: Four trips. I will pay for four. Eight hundred for the lot, and I will call that fair.

job_avenida.speaker: Renzo
job_avenida.text: Eight hundred is fair. Is fair enough?

options: Carry it free; she will owe you

effects.banner: Haggled: P1,000, but it cost 15 extra minutes
Aling Cora owes you a favor

job_avenida.text: Four trips. The rain soaks the katsa and the katsa soaks Renzo. On the last stack a bolt of black cloth slides loose and unrolls across the wet pavement: heavy, close-woven, the exact weave that wraps Lola's watch.

job_avenida.speaker: Aling Cora
job_avenida.text: Eh, that one is not for sale. Old stock. Your Lola orders a bolt every year on the same date, and has for forty years. She has never once said what for.

job_avenida.speaker: Renzo
job_avenida.text: Every year. On the same date.

job_avenida.speaker: Aling Cora
job_avenida.text: Four trips. Done. Go, go, before it floods the stall.

job_pandacan.text: Pandacan. The depot sits behind a fish-processing plant that stopped processing sometime in the nineties. Its cold room still hums.

job_pandacan.speaker: Kuya Efren
job_pandacan.text: You're the Reyes boy. Compressor head's in the back. And do not open the walk-in. It is not on the inventory.

job_pandacan.speaker: Renzo
job_pandacan.text: People only warn you about a door once they have opened it.
The compressor hums on a note that is almost a word.

job_pandacan.speaker: Renzo
job_pandacan.text: The walk-in door is warm. Not cold. Warm.

effects.banner: Frostbitten fingers: -6 HP at the next fight

job_pandacan.text: Frost writes itself across the inside of the door as he pushes: not words. Numbers. 4:17. 4:17. 4:17, in nine different handwritings.
The room is empty except for a chair and a stopped wall clock. Its glass is fogged from the inside.

job_pandacan.speaker: Kuya Efren
job_pandacan.text: I told you. Every Quiapo watchmaker who ever fixed that clock ended up sitting in that chair. I just keep the ice.

job_pandacan.speaker: Renzo
job_pandacan.text: He is not joking, and I am not going to ask how long he has been keeping it.

job_pandacan.speaker: Kuya Efren
job_pandacan.text: Good. Smart boys live to be old men who complain about the weather.
Ninety minutes, a compressor head and fifteen hundred pesos later, the Honda coughs back into the rain.

church_arrival.text: The courtyard of Quiapo Church at noon: devotees pressed between candle stalls and mango sellers, the rain doing nothing to thin them.

church_arrival.speaker: Renzo
church_arrival.text: The parcel is taped shut, no name, and pays more than any parcel should. I am carrying it to the one place in Manila no one would think to hide anything.

dusk_choice.text: Dusk. The Avenida is a brown river, and behind Renzo the church bells ring six, a heartbeat late. Ahead, two roads lead to Evangelista Street.

dusk_choice.speaker: Renzo
dusk_choice.text: The lit way is the long way: Carriedo, the overpass, the checkpoint where Valdez's cousins drink. Forty minutes of lamps.

dusk_choice.speaker: Renzo
dusk_choice.text: The short way is the alley behind the bakeries. Ten minutes. No lamps.

dusk_choice.speaker: Renzo
dusk_choice.text: Dante said stay on lit streets. Dante is a stranger on a phone.

options: Take the shortcut through the alley
Take the lit road, as Dante said

effects.banner: The shortcut saves half an hour
Dante would approve of the lit road

dusk_choice.text: Carriedo is closed. A bus has stalled in the flood, and an Aevum checkpoint is turning every rider back.

dusk_choice.speaker: Renzo
dusk_choice.text: Aevum Filipinas. Private security. Why are they checking couriers' pockets?
The pocket watch ticks once, loud as a dropped coin, against his ribs. The nearest guard's head turns.

dusk_choice.speaker: Renzo
dusk_choice.text: Not here. Not that. Turn the bike around.

act1_hook.text: The alley behind Evangelista Street swallows the Honda's headlight.

act1_hook.speaker: Renzo
act1_hook.text: No lamps. No witnesses. Dante said stay on lit streets. Dante is not the one with a noon deadline.

act1_hook.speaker: Renzo
act1_hook.text: Every other road is closed. Dante said stay on lit streets. He didn't say what to do when the lit streets stop.

alley_intro.text: Quiapo, dusk. The watch ticks against Renzo's palm, backward and patient: one last delivery, down the alley behind Evangelista Street.

alley_intro.speaker: Renzo
alley_intro.text: The invoice says Gat. Dizon, Bodega 9. The ink is too fresh and the signature is traced. A fake. Great.

alley_intro.speaker: Renzo
alley_intro.text: Lola has never let anyone else touch this watch, and tonight she's sending it to a stranger at the end of an alley. That is not easy money. That is a goodbye.

alley_search.text: Monobloc chairs stacked behind a bakery, tin overhangs sweating rain, one streetlight that flickers like it is thinking about quitting.

alley_search.speaker: Renzo
alley_search.text: The invoice says Bodega 9 has a blue stripe on its door.
Three doors have blue on them. Two of them are lying.

options: The bakery's back door (smells of bread)
The door with the dented shutter
The door with the fresh paint (still wet)

alley_search.text: A baker's apprentice opens, flour to the elbows, and shakes his head fast.

alley_search.speaker: Baker's apprentice
alley_search.text: No Dizon here, sir. No blue door. Please, the alley after six is not for us. Last week the bins were torn open from the inside.
The shutter dents inward under his knuckles, cracked from the other side a long time ago by something that wanted out.
The stripe is wet because someone wanted it to look fresh. Behind it hangs a padlock with a corporate seal: a chevron inside a circle.

alley_search.speaker: Renzo
alley_search.text: Aevum's chevron. On a lock in Quiapo.
A smear of black oil runs along the wall from the fire escape, under the streetlight, to Renzo's boots. It is still warm.
The watch ticks backward faster. The oil trail points up.

alley_search.speaker: Renzo
alley_search.text: The watch is racing. The oil points up.

options: Follow the trail up the fire escape
Wait by the door with the watch in your fist

effects.banner: Your voice echoes. Something above answers.

alley_search.text: Halfway up the iron stairs he sees it: a shape folded into the corner of the landing, too many joints, two red eyes opening in the dark.

alley_search.speaker: Renzo
alley_search.text: Back down. Back down. Back down.

alley_search.speaker: Renzo
alley_search.text: Whatever comes, it comes at me, not at my back.
'Renzo?' says a voice from the fire escape, in Lola's own cadence. The lamps die one by one.

alley_ambush.text: Rusted iron screams overhead. Something heavy lands in the dark.

alley_ambush.speaker: Renzo
alley_ambush.text: Diyos ko... the lamps, they all went out. And that thing... it was on the fire escape the whole time.

alley_ambush.speaker: Renzo
alley_ambush.text: All I've got is a balisong... Walang atrasan. Walang atrasan. Say it like you mean it, Renzo.

after_fight_alley.text: The smoke is gone. It leaves one thing on the asphalt: a clamp of black alloy no bigger than a thumb, still blinking.

after_fight_alley.speaker: Renzo
after_fight_alley.text: A telemetry tag. Clamped to its ear. Nobody tags a monster they haven't been watching.

options: Take it (evidence, but it may be tracking you)

after_fight_alley.speaker: Renzo
after_fight_alley.text: It pings once against my palm. A green light. I may have just told someone exactly where I am.
The tag dies with a small, offended chirp.

after_fight_alley.speaker: Renzo
after_fight_alley.text: Whoever was listening just lost the signal. They'll want to know why.
The watch is burning through the cloth. Its hands run backward through a minute that already happened.

after_fight_alley.speaker: Renzo
after_fight_alley.text: How long was I out there? Four minutes? Forty?

gate_ram.text: Headlights. An engine screaming straight down the alley. The chained gate behind Renzo is the only way out, and it is about to stop being a gate.

gate_ram.speaker: Dante
gate_ram.text: RENZO! Get in the van! Lola's seal is broken. That thing isn't supposed to be out of the Veil!

gate_ram.speaker: Renzo
gate_ram.text: Dante?! You... you crashed through the gate. Of course you did.

gate_ram.speaker: Dante
gate_ram.text: Door's open. Decide fast. I cannot make small talk with Aevum two streets behind me.

gate_ram.speaker: Renzo
gate_ram.text: A van with a stranger, or the Honda in the flood?

options: Run for it on the Honda

gate_ram.text: The Honda stalls in the flood two blocks on. The van rolls up alongside, wipers going.

van_talk.text: The van smells of diesel, gin and wet dog. Dante drives like the road owes him money.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Name's Dante. I fixed your grandfather's bicycle in 1996 and he never paid me. He paid me in watches, and I never fixed those either.

van_talk.speaker: Renzo
van_talk.text: You knew Lolo.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Knew him. Drank with him. He was a bad drinker and a worse liar, and the best watchmaker in Manila.

van_talk.speaker: Renzo
van_talk.text: Three questions. One ride.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Aswang. A real one. Old, patient, not hungry for anything you would call food. And someone fine-tuned it to find you.

van_talk.speaker: Renzo
van_talk.text: Fine-tuned.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Your Lola keeps a door shut. Not a door door. A door in the city. The watch is the lock. Every time it ticks backward, the lock holds.

van_talk.speaker: Renzo
van_talk.text: And when it ticks forward?

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Then the door opens.
A long beat. The wipers. The rain.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: It has not ticked forward in twenty-six years.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: You shouldn't. That is the first smart thing you have said all night.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: But I lit the lamp when your Lolo went out that night, and I am the one who kept the river off your Lola's doorstep since. I am not asking you to trust me. I am asking you to stay in the van.
Rain drums the roof. Somewhere behind them a siren with no flashing light goes quiet.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Hands. Let me see the watch.

van_talk.speaker: Renzo
van_talk.text: He's asking for the one thing I was told never to open.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Balete wood and cold iron. She gave it to you.
He does not touch it. He looks at it the way you look at an old photograph.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Fine. Keep it. But if it starts to sing, you will show me.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: So. Where do we go?

van_talk.speaker: Renzo
van_talk.text: Dante's workshop, or back to Lola?

options: Tondo: Dante's workshop (safe, away from Quiapo)
Back to Quiapo: Lola is alone

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Not yet. If Aevum is in Quiapo they are already inside the shop, and walking in tonight gets you both killed. Tondo. Then we plan.

van_talk.speaker: Renzo
van_talk.text: He is right. I hate that he is right.

van_talk.speaker: Dante
van_talk.text: Good call. Tondo it is.

after_fight.text: The van is quiet. Renzo takes the watch out. It is spinning backward at three times its pace, and the rain on the windshield stops falling, and begins to run upward.

after_fight.speaker: Dante
after_fight.text: ...Kid. I saw that. The rain fell upward for three seconds, and your pocket was glowing. You rewound something.

after_fight.speaker: Renzo
after_fight.text: It does that. It has been doing that all day.

after_fight.speaker: Dante
after_fight.text: No. It does not. Hold on to that thing, Renzo. It has just done what it was built to do, and the people who built it are very much alive.

safehouse_arrival.text: Tondo. A chop shop under a zinc roof, rain on the sheets like gravel. The van stops, and the shop's one working fluorescent tube remembers to turn on.

safehouse_arrival.speaker: Dante
safehouse_arrival.text: Sit on the crate. Not that one, that one is a bomb. Joke. Mostly.

safehouse_arrival.speaker: Dante
safehouse_arrival.text: They stop when you give them something to do. Hold this.
A torque wrench, heavier than it looks. It does help.

safehouse_arrival.speaker: Renzo
safehouse_arrival.text: Dante is holding a bottle of gin and a first-aid kit.

safehouse_arrival.speaker: Dante
safehouse_arrival.text: Don't pour it on the cuts unless you want to pass out. Drink it. Then I pour it. The claws carry corpse-rot.

safehouse_arrival.speaker: Renzo
safehouse_arrival.text: It tastes like a car battery. It helps. I hate that it helps.

safehouse_arrival.speaker: Dante
safehouse_arrival.text: Pride. Your Lolo had it too. Use the clean side of the cloth, not the rag.

safehouse_arrival.speaker: Dante
safehouse_arrival.text: Lola is alive. Alive and loud, if I know her. We will find out where she is. First you need to be a person who can walk through a door.
Dante spreads a map of Quiapo across the hood of a motorcycle. Red crosses. Black vans. Chevrons in circles.

safehouse_arrival.speaker: Dante
safehouse_arrival.text: Before I explain anything: open the cloth. Lola told you the invoice was in the cloth.

envelope_open.text: The watch lies on the bench between them. The black cloth it came wrapped in is still folded in Renzo's pocket.

envelope_open.speaker: Renzo
envelope_open.text: Do not open it on the way. I have gotten as far as 'the way' is going to let me.
Between the weave and the lining: a traced invoice for Gat. Dizon, Bodega 9, signed in a hand that is not a hand. And a thicker envelope, wax-sealed with a chevron inside a circle.

envelope_open.speaker: Dante
envelope_open.text: That is not the church's seal. That is Aevum's.

envelope_open.speaker: Renzo
envelope_open.text: The sacristan's envelope. The one he slid across the stone this morning. I put it in my pocket and never opened it.

envelope_open.speaker: Renzo
envelope_open.text: A wax seal with Aevum's chevron.
A lease notice on Aevum letterhead: 'Lot 14, Carriedo Street (Reyes Watch Repair & Herbs) is subject to acquisition under Resolution 417. Occupant: Rosa Reyes. Basis: custodianship of Item 4-17-A.'

envelope_open.speaker: Dante
envelope_open.text: That is you. That is the watch. That is what this whole city has been counting toward.
Dante breaks the seal with his thumbnail, reads, and goes the color of old plaster.

envelope_open.speaker: Dante
envelope_open.text: Item 4-17-A. Custodianship. They are not after Lola, Renzo. They are after what she is holding.
Folded behind the notice: a small, creased photograph. Lola at thirty, holding a baby who is not Renzo's father. On the back, in Lolo's hand: 'Siya ang susunod.' She is the next.

envelope_open.speaker: Dante
envelope_open.text: I do not know. I swear on every wrench in this shop, I do not know.

envelope_open.speaker: Renzo
envelope_open.text: He is telling the truth. That is what frightens me.
At the far end of the bench, the scanner clears its throat in static.

hound_intro.text: The shop lights die at once. On the skylight, one by one, four metal feet touch the zinc.

hound_intro.speaker: Dante
hound_intro.text: They found us anyway. Aevum does not give up a signal; it only changes the dog.
The skylight shatters. Something with a red lens drops through it and lands on the bench, scattering maps, wrenches and the watch.

hound_intro.speaker: Dante
hound_intro.text: Hound! Behind me, kid, I have to hold the breaker or the whole block goes dark and every van in Tondo hears it!

hound_intro.speaker: Renzo
hound_intro.text: He cannot leave the breaker. It's me. It's just me and the watch.
The watch, in Renzo's fist, begins to count backward before he asks it to.

hound_after.text: The hound's lens cracks, spits sparks, and goes dark. The safehouse lights stutter back on.

hound_after.speaker: Dante
hound_after.text: I felt that. The whole shop went cold for a second, and then everything the hound did to us unwound itself. That is the watch?

hound_after.speaker: Dante
hound_after.text: Then it is awake, and so is everyone who has been waiting twenty-six years for it to be.

hound_after.speaker: Renzo
hound_after.text: He says it like a diagnosis.

act3_big.speaker: Dante
act3_big.text: Quiapo is two choices. Now, with a wrench, a watch and a lot of nerve. Or an hour with me, a plan, and a very bad map.

act3_big.speaker: Dante
act3_big.text: Then take this. A taser. It is what I have. Don't let the watch tell you what to do.

act3_big.speaker: Dante
act3_big.text: Good. Their transport leaves for Taguig at midnight. We catch the van at the Bonifacio crossing, with the watch and a plan.
The watch jumps in Renzo's hand.

domeng_stall.text: Mang Domeng's candle stall, behind the church. Wax drips in the rain faster than he can sell it.

domeng_stall.speaker: Mang Domeng
domeng_stall.text: Renzo! You're soaked. Come, come under the tarp. The saints can spare a minute.

domeng_stall.speaker: Renzo
domeng_stall.text: I can't stay, Mang Domeng. I have a parcel for the undercroft by noon.

domeng_stall.speaker: Mang Domeng
domeng_stall.text: Then a minute, only a minute. Forty years I have lit candles for people who wanted a different life. You know what they all ask for?

domeng_stall.speaker: Renzo
domeng_stall.text: He is waiting for me to guess.

domeng_stall.speaker: Mang Domeng
domeng_stall.text: Money, everyone says. But no. Money is what they ask for out loud.

domeng_stall.speaker: Mang Domeng
domeng_stall.text: Safety, yes. That is what the old ones ask for. The young ones are braver. Or dumber.

domeng_stall.speaker: Mang Domeng
domeng_stall.text: Time. Yes. You have your Lolo's face when you say it. He asked for it every week, until the week he stopped asking.

domeng_stall.speaker: Mang Domeng
domeng_stall.text: Your Lola paid for forty candles last Thursday. In advance. She has never done that.

domeng_stall.speaker: Renzo
domeng_stall.text: Forty candles. In advance. Someone who plans to be gone.

domeng_stall.speaker: Mang Domeng
domeng_stall.text: Take one. For the road. It is only a candle, but sometimes that is a lot.
A thin white candle, still warm from the mold. Renzo tucks it into the strap of his helmet.

tow_confrontation.text: Noon. The bells ring twelve, a heartbeat late, and a tow truck with no plates backs up to the shop's curb.
Two men in matching rain jackets: Valdez's cousins. One of them is already hooking the Honda's front wheel.

tow_confrontation.speaker: R. Valdez
tow_confrontation.text: Reyes. Eleven hundred pesos short on the third notice, and a bike that was never yours to begin with. I would call it a courtesy, but I don't.

tow_confrontation.speaker: Renzo
tow_confrontation.text: I paid what I could. I will have the rest tomorrow.

tow_confrontation.speaker: R. Valdez
tow_confrontation.text: Tomorrow is a word for people who can afford it.

tow_confrontation.speaker: Renzo
tow_confrontation.text: They have the Honda hooked. I have a balisong and a watch.

options: Pay what you have and beg

tow_confrontation.text: Renzo steps off the curb before the thought finishes.

tow_confrontation.speaker: R. Valdez
tow_confrontation.text: Ay, ay. A hero. Boys, teach him what a notice means.

tow_confrontation.speaker: R. Valdez
tow_confrontation.text: The courtesy of a rule is that I do not enjoy it. Take the money and be quiet.
The tow truck pulls away with the Honda's taillight blinking through the rain.

tow_confrontation.speaker: Renzo
tow_confrontation.text: Another debt. Another number on the book. Lola will count it before I say a word.

tow_after.text: The cousins limp away, one holding the other up. The Honda hangs half off its hook, and the tow truck's engine idles, undecided.

tow_after.speaker: R. Valdez
tow_after.text: ...You are more trouble than the shop is worth, Reyes. Keep the bike. This once. The notice stays.

tow_after.speaker: Renzo
tow_after.text: This once. He means it. He also means the next time won't be a courtesy.
Renzo unhooks the wheel himself, hands shaking, knuckles split.

van_chase_intro.text: The van tears out of the alley with a crack of splintered chain. Behind them, headlights without a plate, doing sixty in a thirty zone.

van_chase_intro.speaker: Dante
van_chase_intro.text: Aevum! Two vans! Kid, I drive, you navigate. Left, always left. The flood is on our side tonight.

van_chase_intro.speaker: Renzo
van_chase_intro.text: The Avenida is a river. We are not driving on it. We are driving through it.

van_chase_intro.speaker: Dante
van_chase_intro.text: Tell me when the lanes open. Steer us through the traffic. If I hit a jeepney, your Lolo comes back to haunt us both.

bodega_nine.text: Bodega 9's door is not locked. It is not even closed. The blue stripe has been painted over with a thin coat of grey, and the bodega behind it breathes out cold.

bodega_nine.speaker: Renzo
bodega_nine.text: Gat. Dizon. Nobody comes to a door like this to sign for a parcel.
A single bulb burns over a workbench. On it, a row of stopped clocks and a ledger. At the bench, in a chair that fits him too well, sits a man in a good suit. He has been dead for a while.

bodega_nine.speaker: Renzo
bodega_nine.text: Dizon. Whoever delivered this watch to him wouldn't have been bringing it for a signature.

bodega_nine.speaker: Renzo
bodega_nine.text: The dead man's hand is closed around something.

options: Back out and call it in

bodega_nine.text: In his palm: a brass key stamped with a number, 4-17, and a tiny watchmaker's screwdriver, worn bright.

bodega_nine.speaker: Renzo
bodega_nine.text: A watchmaker's screwdriver. Dizon was one of us.
The ledger lists names and dates, back to 1898. Every entry ends the same way: 'Delivered. Awaiting the heir.' The last line is in fresh ink: 'Reyes, R. Tonight.'

bodega_nine.speaker: Renzo
bodega_nine.text: Heir. He was waiting for me. He was waiting for me, and something killed him for it.

bodega_nine.speaker: Renzo
bodega_nine.text: I'm not going to be the next name in this ledger. Not like this.
Behind Renzo, the alley's last streetlight goes out.

lola_message.text: Dante's scanner coughs, and a voice that is not Aevum's comes through the static: an old woman, calm as a tea kettle.

lola_message.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_message.text: Renzo. If you are hearing this, the hound found you, or the watch did. Either way, you are breathing, and that is enough.

lola_message.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_message.text: I recorded this on Dante's old tape. Do not be angry with him. I made him promise to wait until you were in his van.

lola_message.speaker: Renzo
lola_message.text: You knew he would find me.

lola_message.speaker: Dante
lola_message.text: I knew she would call it. I just did not think it would be this soon.

lola_message.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_message.text: Ask me to apologise, and I will not. Ask me why, and I will tell you when I can look at you. There is a place on the Pasig where the river tastes of rust. Go there when this is over.

lola_message.speaker: Renzo
lola_message.text: Her voice is calm. That is what makes it hard.

options: Say nothing. Listen to her breathe.
Ask Dante to stop the tape

lola_message.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_message.text: Good. Keep the watch close. It does not lie. It only counts.
In the static behind her, a door opens and a man says her name.
Dante stops it, wordless. Rain on the zinc. The tape's last two seconds hang in the air like a held breath.

lola_message.speaker: Lola Rosa
lola_message.text: Tell Renzo I put the third drawer on the left back in order. He will understand when he is older. No. When he is ready.

agent_offer.text: The scanner clears its throat again. This time the voice is smooth, practised, and very polite.

agent_offer.speaker: Aevum guard
agent_offer.text: Mr. Reyes. I apologise for the hound. It was a clumsy introduction. My name is Tolentino, Aevum Filipinas, Custodianship division.

agent_offer.speaker: Aevum guard
agent_offer.text: We invited her. She declined. Eleven times. We are good at patience; we are less good at being told no.

agent_offer.speaker: Aevum guard
agent_offer.text: Give us the watch. We will return Mrs. Reyes to her shop, forgive the lease, and settle the Valdez debt. Tonight.

agent_offer.speaker: Renzo
agent_offer.text: Everything I have been counting toward since six this morning, offered in one sentence.

agent_offer.speaker: Renzo
agent_offer.text: The deal is real. That is what is wrong with it.

options: Stall: ask for proof she is alive
Ask what the watch actually does

agent_offer.speaker: Aevum guard
agent_offer.text: A pity. We will not ask a third time.

agent_offer.speaker: Aevum guard
agent_offer.text: Proof. Of course. Mrs. Reyes, would you say something?

agent_offer.speaker: Lola Rosa
agent_offer.text: Do not give them the watch.

agent_offer.speaker: Aevum guard
agent_offer.text: She is stubborn. That is a family trait.

agent_offer.speaker: Aevum guard
agent_offer.text: It does what it was built to do: it keeps a door shut. We would like to open it. There is a great deal of power on the other side, Mr. Reyes, and a great deal of money.

agent_offer.speaker: Dante
agent_offer.text: He's reading from a pamphlet. Hang up.
The line goes to static, and then, softly, to a ticking.

dante_story.text: Dante pours two cups of something that is not tea and hands one over without asking.

dante_story.speaker: Dante
dante_story.text: You want the night of the flood? The real one, not the one your Lola tells?

dante_story.speaker: Dante
dante_story.text: June third, 1998. The river rose at three. By four it was in your Lolo's shop, up past the counter. I was carrying jars to the second floor when I saw him.

dante_story.speaker: Dante
dante_story.text: He was standing in the middle of the flood with the watch in both hands. Calm. Like a man at a christening.

dante_story.speaker: Dante
dante_story.text: The hands went backward. And the water went with them. Down the stairs, out the door, back into the street, like a rug being pulled by a very polite giant.

dante_story.speaker: Dante
dante_story.text: That is what it did. And it took four minutes and seventeen seconds, Renzo, and your Lolo aged ten years in them. I counted.

dante_story.speaker: Renzo
dante_story.text: 4:17. Not a time of day. A length of time. Four minutes and seventeen seconds.

dante_story.speaker: Dante
dante_story.text: He never touched it again. Never told her why. I never told her either. The day she found out I knew, she handed me the van keys and said: 'when the boy needs you.'

dante_story.speaker: Dante
dante_story.text: Lola will want to tell you the rest. She should be the one.

dante_story.speaker: Dante
dante_story.text: Fair enough. Some stories wait for better light.
He drinks, and the shop's one working tube hums over the silence between them.

tiyanak_intro.text: Dante locks the safehouse door and kills the lamp. Outside, somewhere in the drainage ditch, a baby is crying.

tiyanak_intro.speaker: Dante
tiyanak_intro.text: Don't. Don't follow it. We are in Tondo, kid. A baby crying in a ditch at night is not a baby.

tiyanak_intro.speaker: Renzo
tiyanak_intro.text: It sounds exactly like a baby. That is the problem.

tiyanak_intro.speaker: Renzo
tiyanak_intro.text: The crying comes in short, wet waves.

options: Throw a stone at the ditch

tiyanak_intro.text: The sound leads to a drain cover warm as skin. The crying stops when he steps on it.
The stone clanks down the ditch. The crying pauses, considers, and begins again, closer.
It does not stop. It comes in under the shutter, a wet little scrape.

tiyanak_intro.speaker: Dante
tiyanak_intro.text: Tiyanak. A baby that was never born, or never named. It learns your sister's voice and wears it. Do not listen to the words.

tiyanak_intro.speaker: Renzo
tiyanak_intro.text: It has Lola's voice. It's saying, 'Anak, help me.'

tiyanak_after.text: Dante exhales, finally, and sets down the wrench he had not realised he was holding.

tiyanak_after.speaker: Dante
tiyanak_after.text: That is the third one this month. Something is feeding them, or something is calling them. I would like not to know which.

tiyanak_after.speaker: Renzo
tiyanak_after.text: It had Lola's voice. It said 'Anak.' I'm going to hear that for a long time.

baker_return.text: The baker's apprentice peeks out from behind the half-open door, flour and fear in equal measure, a paper bag held out in front of him like a shield.

baker_return.speaker: Baker's apprentice
baker_return.text: Sir? Sir, is it gone? I saw the light. I saw the smoke. I saw you.

baker_return.speaker: Baker's apprentice
baker_return.text: Paolo. I... I brought bread. It's what we have. The bins are empty; the thing tore them open last week and the owner blames me.

baker_return.speaker: Renzo
baker_return.text: He is shaking, and he came back anyway.

options: Take the bread and thank him
Tell him to go home and lock the door

effects.banner: You gave away the candle. Someone needed it more

baker_return.speaker: Baker's apprentice
baker_return.text: It's still warm! Pandesal, three hours old. Please eat.

baker_return.speaker: Renzo
baker_return.text: It is the best thing I have eaten all day, and I have eaten nothing all day.

baker_return.speaker: Baker's apprentice
baker_return.text: A candle? From Mang Domeng? ...Thank you. My mother lights one every night. We ran out on Tuesday.

baker_return.speaker: Baker's apprentice
baker_return.text: Yes, sir. Lock it. Three locks. I'll ask the owner for a fourth.
Paolo disappears behind the door. The bolts slide home, one, two, three. Four.

dante_tips.text: The van slows at a red light that has not changed in a decade. Dante drums the wheel.

dante_tips.speaker: Dante
dante_tips.text: That thing nearly had you. You were late on the first one. I saw. You flinched.

dante_tips.speaker: Dante
dante_tips.text: Everything is fast when you stare at the claws. Look at the circle. Tap when it glows.

dante_tips.speaker: Renzo
dante_tips.text: A lesson from a mechanic who hasn't been in a fight in twenty years.

dante_tips.speaker: Dante
dante_tips.text: Three rules. One: you cannot dodge what you are watching, so watch the ring. Two: guard before the big ones, and the numbers on the claw card tell you which are big. Three: a perfect parry is worth ten heals. It charges the watch.

dante_tips.speaker: Dante
dante_tips.text: Good. Then you can teach me.

dante_tips.speaker: Dante
dante_tips.text: Because I used to run bodyguard for a man who would not stop buying cursed furniture. Do not ask what was in the chair.
The light turns green. Neither of them says anything for a block.

aevum_raid.speaker: Renzo
aevum_raid.text: What was that thing? That wasn't a stray. It didn't have bones. It was made of oil and smoke.

aevum_raid.speaker: Dante
aevum_raid.text: That was an Aswang, kid. A real one. Not the bedtime story your lola told you to keep you off Carriedo at night. And it wasn't wild. It had a corporate telemetry tag clamped to its ear.

aevum_raid.speaker: Renzo
aevum_raid.text: A tag? Who tags a demon?

aevum_raid.speaker: Dante
aevum_raid.text: Aevum Filipinas. Private security for the port and half the power grid. They don't kill spirits anymore, Renzo. They harvest them. Now show me the watch.

aevum_raid.speaker: Dante
aevum_raid.text: Petrified balete wood and cold-cast iron. Spinning backward, no mainspring. Kid, this was never meant to be sold. Your grandmother routed it to you the long way because she knew they were closing in.

aevum_raid.speaker: Renzo
aevum_raid.text: She was already packing. The crates. The stopped clocks. The tea. She knew.
Dante's scanner crackles. Aevum chatter, Quiapo sector.

aevum_raid.speaker: Dante
aevum_raid.text: Renzo... while I was pulling you out, they hit Rosa's workshop.

aevum_raid.speaker: Scanner
aevum_raid.text: ...ledger secured. Subject in custody. Transport to Taguig medical, ETA twenty minutes...
